Recent qualitative-coding research supports explicit codebooks, evidence excerpts, and human checks. A [2024 study](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/16094069241231168) requested textual evidence for each assigned code; [2025 work](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1140/epjds/s13688-025-00548-8) emphasizes iterative, human-centered codebook refinement. Applied here, a proposed taxonomy is: choose-now = explicit present acceptance; defer = explicit postponement or unresolved decision; reject = explicit refusal; cannot-assess = insufficient evidence. This is a task-specific synthesis, not an established four-class standard. Keep decision status separate from reason codes; ambiguous statements should remain unresolved rather than becoming negative preferences.

Require every reason code to reference observed feedback and available titles, descriptions, or histories. Record missing metadata separately from demonstrated incompatibility; abstain from unsupported claims about fit, specifications, or user traits. [AbstentionBench (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09038) finds persistent failures on underspecified and unanswerable questions: prompting helps but does not establish reliability. Useful diagnostic measurements therefore include evidence-supported coding coverage, unsupported-claim rate, cannot-assess frequency, and human-adjudicated agreement, each with explicit denominators.

With five users per category, report user-level counts and individual cases; repeated item judgments do not create independent users. [NIST guidance](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/software/dataplot/refman2/auxillar/exacbino.htm) favors exact binomial intervals over normal approximations for small samples. Even 5/5 yields an approximately 48–100% two-sided 95% interval under independent binomial sampling; selected users further limit population interpretation. Treat category patterns as exploratory hypotheses, not calibrated prevalence estimates. Keep these diagnostics separate from the fixed macro validation HR@10 used for model selection.
